message.content:
**Uno – Basic Rules (for a standard 108‑card deck)** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or play all your cards and win the round). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Setup** | • Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face down as the draw pile.
• Turn over the top card to start the discard pile; if it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Sequence** | 1. **Draw** – If you cannot or choose not to play a card, draw one from the draw pile.
2. **Play** – Play one card that matches either the color, number, or symbol of the top discard. If you have no playable card, you may play a Wild or Wild Draw Four (see below).
3. **Discard** – After playing, place the card on the discard pile. | | **Playable Cards** | • **Number cards** – Match by value (e.g., 5 of red can be played on any 5).
• **Action cards** – Must match by color or symbol:
 – *Skip* – Next player loses their turn.
 – *Reverse* – Reverses play direction.
 – *Draw Two* – Next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
 – *Wild* – Player chooses new color.
 – *Wild Draw Four* – Same as Wild, but next player also draws four cards. | | **Special Rules** | • **Drawing** – If the draw pile runs out, reshuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new draw pile.
• **Calling “UNO”** – When you have only one card left, shout “UNO!” before your opponent takes their turn. Failure to call UNO when required results in a penalty: draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points based on the cards remaining in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points each.
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Scoring** | Add the round’s points to the winner’s total. First player to reach 500 points wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of colors** – If you’re holding many cards of a single color, try to get rid of them early so you can switch to a different color later. 2. **Use action cards strategically** – Save a *Draw Two* or *Reverse* for when you think it will give you an advantage (e.g., forcing a strong player to draw). 3. **Watch the discard pile** – Pay attention to what cards are being played; this helps you anticipate which cards you’ll need to hold or discard. 4. **Mind the Wild Draw Four rule** – You can only play a Wild Draw Four if you truly have no matching color. If challenged and found to have a playable card, you must draw four cards instead of the challenger drawing eight. Enjoy playing Uno!
